Action Plan:
1. Viral upper respiratory tract infection / possible early influenza: advise 1–2 days off work, rest, maintain adequate oral hydration, continue paracetamol and ibuprofen as needed (dose/route/frequency not documented). Safety-net: return or call sooner if fever recurs or rises, breathing becomes laboured, chest pain develops, or symptoms persist >7 days.
2. Mild exertional breathlessness associated with current viral illness: monitor; seek review if shortness of breath at rest, wheeze, or decreased exercise tolerance.
3. Work-related stress check-in: patient encouraged to re-present if mood or stress becomes unmanageable.
4. Follow-up: telehealth or in-person review in one week if no improvement.
5. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Reason for visit: Feeling “under the weather” × 4 days.  
• HPI:  
  – Day 1–2: sore throat with painful swallowing → improving.  
  – Day 2: clear rhinorrhoea and nasal congestion.  
  – Day 3–4: dry, persistent cough; night sweats; generalized fatigue; intermittent headaches; myalgias.  
  – Fever only first 1–2 days; relieved by paracetamol/ibuprofen.  
  – Mild exertional dyspnoea; none at rest; no chest pain.  
  – Denies nausea, vomiting, rash, ear pain, visual changes, bowel/urinary problems.  
• Past medical history: None reported.  
• Medications: Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented); Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Allergies: No known drug allergies.  
• Family history: Grandmother – type 2 diabetes; great-grandfather – eczema.  
• Social history: Lives alone; accountant; episodic cigar smoking at company events; social alcohol; mild work stress, mood good.

Objective:
• Telehealth consultation; no physical examination or vitals performed/documented.  
• No investigations performed.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Upper respiratory tract infection / viral illness
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Viral upper respiratory tract infection (common cold) – High likelihood (DDx item 1, “High”).
   - Differential diagnosis:
     • Influenza – Medium (DDx item 2); supporting systemic symptoms.  
     • COVID-19 (mild) – Medium (DDx item 3); night sweats, exertional dyspnoea; no anosmia.  
     • Acute bacterial sinusitis – Low; duration <7 days, clear discharge.  
     • Streptococcal pharyngitis – Low; throat pain resolving, presence of cough/rhinorrhoea.
   - Investigations planned: None at this stage; consider COVID-19 test if regional guidance warrants or if symptoms worsen (not discussed in consult).
   - Treatment planned:
     • Rest 1–2 days, hydration.  
     • Continue paracetamol and ibuprofen as needed (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
     • Symptomatic care (e.g., saline nasal spray, throat lozenges) if desired (not explicitly discussed).  
     • Safety-net advice as above.
   - Relevant referrals: None.

2. Mild exertional dyspnoea
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Likely secondary to current viral illness/congestion.
   - Differential diagnosis: Pulmonary embolism (very low likelihood per DDx “V” ‑ opposing evidence: no risk factors, no pleuritic pain) – included for completeness.
   - Investigations planned: None now; urgent review if dyspnoea worsens.
   - Treatment planned: Monitor; as Issue 1 resolves, expect improvement.

3. Work-related stress (preventive)
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Normal occupational stress; mood unaffected.
   - Differential diagnosis: Adjustment-related stress (low).  
   - Treatment planned: Patient advised to seek support if stress/mood issues arise.
   - Referrals: Consider mental health services if future need identified.

Quality checks:
• Missing expected elements: Vitals, physical examination findings, medication dose/route/frequency, vaccination status (including COVID-19), and recent COVID-19 testing history not elicited.  
• Internal conflicts: None identified between transcript and DDx.  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; occasional minor interruptions but clinical content intact.
